original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.

actual_scope: In the six-source, all-63-mask universal dirty-connector model, add a parametrized source-hyperedge family z += sum_{j in S} B_j x_j for 4 <= |S| <= 6, with read-only sources and full price one dispatch plus |S| source additions. Prove the exact charged batch floor and test the PR #2128 witness as a positive dirty-state control.
scope_change_reason: The suggested joint-query scope is densely claimed, while the connector-alphabet task has one fixed DUO upper construction, one fixed TRIO profile, and an open handoff for a changed connector contract. This refinement changes the operation family from arity two/three to all arities four through six at fixed n=6, and asks for a family-wide additive-price theorem rather than another finite word census.
bottleneck_link: A lower-cost source operation could reduce the paid recursive interface. The optimistic complete price includes dispatch, every constituent source addition, and any implementation surcharge. The result tests whether higher arity alone can improve the full six-source connector profile.
stop_rule: Prove the query-call/readout case split for any number of output readouts, prove W>=16 by singleton expansion, verify the exact positive word and dirty batch schedule, then stop once Q>=140 and total additions>=142 close the additive-price profile. Do not enumerate words after the general floor is proved.
evidence: For each hyperedge S, splitting into |S| singleton toggles retains every original boundary, so W>=f(6)=16. Let M be missing nonzero pairwise prefix differences. Each output needs an even readout count; a missing mask needs at least four reads, so R>=126+2M. The published exact r((C2)^6)=14 forces M>=1 for k=12,13; for k<=11, M>=63-binomial(k,2); for k>=14, R>=126 suffices. Thus Q=k+R>=140 for all k and any arity. Also W+R>=142. The PR #2128 witness attains (Q,W+R)=(140,142). No supplier or kappa result.
author: Cinna Davis
ai_assistance: Substantial OpenAI Codex assistance in task selection, mathematical derivation, verifier implementation and drafting. The 14-call/16-add witness belongs to Aaron Wang/Navinor PR #2128; f(6)=16 is predecessor work in research/universal-connector-six-source; the basis-size 14 result is Volodymyr Gavrylkiv 2017. No independent human review is claimed.

open_questions.question: Can one concrete selected-supplier interface implement an arity-four-or-higher source hyperedge at a total charge below the sum of its source taps?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Only a realizable subadditive charge escapes the exact additive-price profile floor proved here.
open_questions.first_step: Choose one existing supplier frame, instantiate a four-source hyperedge on its literal registers, derive its complete native routing/frame/precision invoice, and compare against four separate source reads.
open_questions.blocked_by: No admitted physical realization of the six-source abstract connector interface is currently available.
